fields.label: Your story
fields.sample:
Ten years ago, on a summer evening, we said “yes.” Since then we’ve collected two cities, three homes, countless morning coffees and never-ending conversations.
There were hard days too; each time, we stood on the same side. Looking back today, it’s the laughter we remember most.
This issue is a short archive of ten years, and a promise for the years ahead.

fields.label: Thank-you message
fields.sample: Thank you to everyone who has stood by us for ten years, sharing our joys and our troubles. Here’s to many more years, together!

elements.name: Haber başlığı

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
The couple who said “yes” in a small garden years ago are get­ting ready to cel­e­brate their an­niver­sary with the same ex­cite­ment as on day one. Our paper is once again pre­sent­ing its wedding-day story, pulled from the ar­chive, to­geth­er with a brief run­down of the years since.
According to ar­chive records, the couple have since gone through two cities, three homes and count­less morn­ing cof­fees. Most of their ar­gu­ments have been over who gets the remote and whether to va­ca­tion in the moun­tains or by the sea; nei­ther has been set­tled yet.
Those close to them say the two still laugh to­geth­er like on the first day and have stood on the same side even in the hard­est times. We have learned that the cel­e­bra­tion will be held in the very garden where they mar­ried, once again sur­round­ed by their loved ones.

elements.name: Kupür başlığı
elements.text: Young couple tied the knot last night

elements.name: Kupür metni
elements.text: MODA — Last night, two young people joined their lives in a wed­ding cer­e­mo­ny held in a small garden. Guests said the smile on the bride’s face “lit up the whole evening.” The groom’s voice was heard trem­bling during the vows, while the bride could barely hold back her laugh­ter. At the party, which went on late into the night, the first dance was re­peat­ed three times at the guests’ in­sis­tence. Our paper wishes the young couple a life­time of hap­pi­ness.

elements.name: Kronoloji metni

elements.name: Arşiv notu
elements.text: Some of the clip­pings on this page came off the fridge door, some from an old shoe­box, and the most pre­cious from the bride’s mother’s hand­bag. The dates on the backs of the photos were hand­writ­ten; some have faded, but none of their sto­ries has been for­got­ten. Our ar­chive is always open to read­ers who can help fill in the miss­ing shots.

elements.name: Tanık sözü
elements.text: “My hand shook as I signed; you’d think I was the one getting married.”

elements.name: Tanık metni
elements.text: That day I brought two ball­point pens in case one didn’t work. Both worked, but I still tell the story of the pen that wouldn’t write. It’s a better story.

elements.name: Tanık sözü
elements.text: “Years have passed, and they still laugh at the same joke.”

elements.name: Tanık metni
elements.text: Sunday break­fasts still bring the same debate: does men­e­men get onions or not? These days I just put two pans on the stove.

elements.name: Tanık sözü
elements.text: “Thanks to the laughter from their balcony, I never needed an alarm.”

elements.name: Tanık metni
elements.text: I lived across from their first home. Every morn­ing at the same hour, the smell of coffee; every evening, music. They were the best neigh­bors.

elements.name: Sözler
elements.text:
1. We’ll take turns making the morning coffee; for real this time.
2. We’ll settle arguments before going to sleep.
3. At least once a year, we’ll go somewhere we’ve never been.
4. The remote goes to one of us on odd days and the other on even days.
5. We’ll keep laughing at old photos every year.
6. We agree to postpone the menemen debate forever.
7. We officially recognize the cat as the true owner of the house.

elements.text: Same day, same garden, with you again. Subscription is free and for life; the only condition is to bring a laugh every year.

elements.name: Rehber spotu
elements.text: Tradition says every year has its own gift. Our suggestion for this year: a tin box holding the sweetest notes of ten years.

elements.name: Mektuplar
elements.text:
“Read­ing my par­ents’ wed­ding story in a news­pa­per ten years later is very strange and very lovely. I hung this issue on my bed­room wall.” — Their daughter
“I was the one who made them repeat the first dance three times. I’ll keep my word this year, too.” — The best man
“I kindly ask you to an­nounce who’s right about whose turn it is to make the coffee.” — A reader
“I took the wed­ding photos; I still have the neg­a­tives. Come pick them up al­ready.” — Their pho­tog­ra­pher friend
“Writing on behalf of their cat: as the true owner of the house, I ap­prove this issue. Mind the feed­ing time.” — The cat
“Ten years ago I made the wed­ding cake. This year the recipe is the same, with twice the love.” — Nesrin, the pastry chef

elements.name: İlan 2
elements.text: The top tier of the wed­ding cake. Al­leged­ly hidden in the freez­er.

elements.name: İlan 3
elements.text: The key to our first home. Its key­chain has a little cat, as mis­chievous as its owner.

elements.name: İlan 4
elements.text: A box of old let­ters. Not up for trade, not even for a life­time of new mem­o­ries.

elements.name: İlan 5
elements.text: The remote-control duty roster has been posted on the fridge door. Please comply.

elements.name: İlan 6
elements.text: Every memory from ten years. No asking the price; just listen.

elements.name: İlan 7
elements.text: Our wit­ness says: “I stand by my sig­na­ture.” Here’s to many more!

elements.name: İlan 8
elements.text: Guests coming to the cel­e­bra­tion are kindly asked to bring an old photo each.

elements.name: İlan 9
elements.text: The wed­ding album: week­ends only, and only to family elders.

elements.name: İlan 10
elements.text: Be­tween the sofa cush­ions: three re­motes, two ear­rings and a wed­ding in­vi­ta­tion.

elements.name: İlan 11
elements.text: Course in menemen-making com­pro­mise. In­struc­tors: the bride and groom.

elements.name: İlan 12
elements.text: Ex­pe­ri­enced ar­chiv­ist wanted for the years ahead. Moth­ers pre­ferred.
